evidenceFlow.title: Matched-day aggregation
evidenceFlow.detail: scripts/build_early_voting_comparison.py --cutoff-date 2026-10-31; exact site mapping; ACCEPTED early-voting records only. scripts/validate_early_voting_comparison.py reconciles days, scopes and demographics. scripts/audit_campus_figures.py independently recounts campus records and checks source archive/member hashes.

metricDefinitions.label: College-age proxy
metricDefinitions.definition: Source age field 18–24 inclusive. The 18–22 alternative is a sensitivity check; neither is a student enrollment flag.

metricDefinitions.label: Campus site
metricDefinitions.definition: TA - NCSU TALLEY STUDENT CENTER in 2022 and 2024; NCSU WESTERN BLVD BUSINESS SERVICES in 2026.

metricDefinitions.label: Matched-day index
metricDefinitions.definition: 2026 cumulative ballots through day d divided by selected historical year cumulative ballots through day d, multiplied by 100.

metricDefinitions.label: Individual-age share
metricDefinitions.definition: Accepted ballots of the given age divided by all ages at that same year’s campus site, times 100.

metricDefinitions.label: 2024 presidential benchmark
metricDefinitions.definition: For the same first 17 early-voting days: 2026 accepted ballot count divided by 2024 accepted ballot count, times 100; separately for Wake County and campus sites, for all ages and ages 18–24. This is a ballot-volume ratio, not a registered-voter turnout rate, target or forecast.

metricDefinitions.label: Same-day registration versus ballot volume
metricDefinitions.definition: All accepted campus-site early ballots, all ages, over the matched first 17 days. Same-day registration counts records with sdr equal to Y or YES. Share = same-day-registration ballots / all site ballots * 100. Count change = (2026 count / selected baseline count - 1) * 100; share change = 2026 unrounded share - baseline unrounded share, in percentage points. Registration ballots are a subset of all ballots; do not add them. The measure does not identify students or count all new voter registrations. Source cohorts and counts are unchanged.

metricDefinitions.label: Distinct denominators and expanded comparisons
metricDefinitions.definition: Site count = accepted ballots in the selected age group at the campus site. Site age mix = campus-site ballots ages 18–24 / all campus-site ballots * 100. Share of Wake college-age ballots = campus-site ballots ages 18–24 / all Wake ballots ages 18–24 * 100. None is turnout among registered or eligible residents. Expanded comparisons retain both baselines, all three disjoint-or-containing scopes, all-age and overlapping age/registration cohorts; count difference = current - baseline; growth = difference / baseline * 100. Shares use the explicit scope or same-cohort county denominator; differences are unrounded percentage points. Never add containing scopes or overlapping cohorts.

metricDefinitions.label: Growth versus Wake County
metricDefinitions.formula: county_growth_pct = (sum(county age-group ballots in 2026) / sum(county age-group ballots in 2022) - 1) * 100; growth_gap_pp = precinct growth_pct - county_growth_pct
metricDefinitions.definition: A separate count-weighted county benchmark is calculated for each age group from the full Wake County totals, including unmapped precincts. It is not an average of precinct percentages. Both periods use the same full 17-day early-voting periods. Negative means slower growth than Wake even when counts rose; positive means faster growth. Undefined precinct growth stays missing, including zero baselines. Units are percentage points. The campus voting-site comparison uses accepted ballots cast at Talley in 2022 and Western Boulevard in 2026, regardless of home precinct; these are separate populations from the residential polygons.

metricDefinitions.label: Extra ballots
metricDefinitions.definition: Age-group ballots from residents recorded in a precinct, wherever they voted early in Wake. Not restricted to Talley or Western Boulevard. Both years must be observed; missing is not zero.

metricDefinitions.label: Percentage growth
metricDefinitions.definition: Undefined for a missing or zero baseline. Positive 2026 count from a known zero baseline is separately flagged. Dashed map borders identify baselines below 20 ballots; the rank filter defaults to at least 20 for this measure and can be changed. Exact counts remain available.

metricDefinitions.label: Change in age mix
metricDefinitions.formula: age_share_year = age-group ballots / ALL-age ballots from the SAME precinct and year * 100; share_change_pp = unrounded 2026 share - unrounded 2022 share
metricDefinitions.definition: Percentage points compare composition among observed early ballots, not demographic changes in all residents. Every denominator includes all accepted early ballots from that precinct at any Wake location. A zero all-age denominator has no defined share.

metricDefinitions.label: County maps and rankings
metricDefinitions.definition: Both maps use the same fixed color classes and geographic viewport in the selected units. Gold outlines identify 01-23 (current Talley area) and 01-31 (current Western Boulevard area). Rankings include only mapped precinct codes with defined comparisons; largest-change mode sorts by absolute magnitude. Unmapped and missing comparisons remain in the CSV/source rows. Current precinct polygons are not harmonized historical boundaries; changes may reflect boundary, population and voting-pattern changes. Age is not verified student status. These are full-period early-ballot counts, not resident turnout rates or estimates of the move’s effect.

source.label: Wake County GIS voting precinct polygons
source.period: Current downloaded boundary snapshot, not election-year boundary reconstructions
filters: Wake County polygons; all published precincts; GeoJSON WGS84 coordinates

metricDefinitions.label: Precinct outlines
metricDefinitions.definition: Original Wake County GIS PRECINCT codes and GeoJSON geometries from its published layer. The server query uses maxAllowableOffset 0.000015 degrees for browser display. Shapes are projected to Web Mercator by the map; no invented geography or individual addresses.

metricDefinitions.label: Joining counts
metricDefinitions.definition: Join PRECINCT 01-23 in ballot aggregates to GIS code 01-23 by removing only the literal PRECINCT prefix. Historical labels absent from this snapshot remain unmapped, never merged with another precinct. Counts retain their original election-year codes.

metricDefinitions.label: Map shading
metricDefinitions.definition: For the selected year and age band, color is the fraction of accepted early ballots from this precinct cast at Talley in 2022/2024 or Western Boulevard in 2026. Zero differs from unavailable/zero-denominator shares. This is location use, not resident turnout.

caveats: Current outlines are a geographic reference; historical precinct boundaries may differ. Selecting a historical year does not reconstruct its boundaries.
Unmapped precinct codes and unknown labels remain counted in the CSV and full tables; map coverage is disclosed for the selected year and age band.
Only the full 17-day early-voting periods are compared. 2024 was presidential; 2022 and 2026 are midterms.

metricDefinitions.label: Walking distance and time
metricDefinitions.formula: network shortest-path metres + origin connector metres + destination connector metres; time_minutes = metres / selected_pace_metres_per_minute; change = Western − Talley
metricDefinitions.definition: Projected EPSG:32119 metres. Source vertices rounded to 0.01 m; existing vertices on edges are noded within 0.025 m. Line crossings without source vertices and network gaps are not joined. Entrance candidates are within 10 m of the building footprint; one fixed usable mapped entrance nearest the official building point is chosen. Straight entrance connectors may be at most 30 m and cannot cross more than 2.5 m of mapped building footprint. Routes use GIS access points rather than confirmed voting-room doors. Times exclude crossing waits, queues, terrain, closures and indoor travel. No occupancy weighting or causal inference.

caveats: Exploratory network estimates, not navigation or certified accessible routes.
Current network reused for both destinations; no 2022 network reconstruction.
Four included buildings have no usable access connection; distances stay missing.
Only included university housing, not all students or off-campus homes.

source.label: Modeled housing-to-classroom, library and dining route proximity
source.provider: Project model using NC State Enterprise GIS
source.period: Current GIS network; comparison locations labeled 2022/2026, not reconstructed historical traffic
filters: 36 usable housing entrances and 22 usable destination buildings
Teaching = active local GIS Classroom buildings, excluding closed Poe Hall
Libraries = Hill complex (047/A/B/C merged once) and Hunt (783A); dining = GIS Dining buildings plus Talley
One equal weight per usable origin/destination pair; no traffic or enrollment weighting
Default excludes Talley-ending trips from both denominators

metricDefinitions.label: Share of modeled trips near site
metricDefinitions.formula: near_share_pct = count(eligible modeled pairs with minimum route-to-selected-distance-basis <= selected radius) / eligible modeled pair count * 100; basis = whole building footprint (default) or mapped entrance point (optional equal circles)
metricDefinitions.definition: Equal-circle mode uses identical ground radii around mapped GIS entrance points, which are not confirmed voting-room doors. Original footprint mode preserves the earlier whole-building buffer calculation. Distances are computed on full-resolution modeled paths, including short entrance connectors. Purple routes and the paginated review list use the exact same basis, radius and eligible-pair filters as the percentage. Display simplification is at most 1 m; no real pedestrian traffic, enrollment or occupancy data is supplied. The default is the full GIS footprint with the same outward buffer distance at both buildings. Route distances display miles, while proximity zones use meters; calculations retain metres (1 mile = 1609.344 metres).

caveats: No observed student traffic, class schedules, occupancy or destination visitation.
GIS Classroom classification misses teaching inside office/laboratory buildings; dining selection does not include every cafe.
Results depend on destinations, threshold, entrance choice and deterministic shortest routes.
No history reconstruction, visibility model or causal voting inference.
